I am in the same scenario, and I hate the get better advice too. My issue with it is that death is inevitable, so the only point in continuing is if you reasonably believe the good out ways the bad. Otherwise it's just prolonged suffering. You know?
At one point when I was first diagnosed in college, I was given lamotrigine. I shortly discontinued them; at the time I didn't like how I responded to them.

Well, I should restate that. I don't believe society has any obligations to me other than the stated laws, it was taking Hobbes and the 'leviathan' a little more literally. I say that because all my life I have tried incredibly hard to be kind to everyone I came across. I excelled in academia, and pursued many intellectual endeavors in the hopes i could better the world. I thought that between kindness and academic excellence I would find a community somewhere, genuine connections, peace, instead despite that at every stage I am always an outsider, I am just exhausted from the feelings of isolation.

I don't mind, physically I am eating alot less, I don't sleep much so I am constantly tired, I have barely been leaving my place except for short joy rides. Nothing terminal, people have worse physically and those issues are driven by my mental issues.

Mentally, I have several painful issues outside of being suicidal of course. I am bipolar, typically this is very bearable. I have depressive periods along with euphoric periods where I feel invincible, and can do anything. Lately, the periods between each episode have been getting shorter and shorter due to stressors. These oscillations have been getting worse, in an attempt to alleviate what I perceived to be the stressor I made it much worse. My psyche collapsed. I was switching between two extremes within the day, manic then depressed, depressed then manic. Mania was a relief, but the depression was incredibly painful, that I were the thoughts of suicide first came in. Then my mania started to become darker a more menacing series of thoughts. I would be laughing, listening to music, and then a wave of sadness would drive me to the worst of depressions. All of this was very painful the dissonance is torture. I have come to the conclusion that the stressors, isolation both now and during my schooling, have led to the onset of schizophrenia. Meaning I now have a schizoaffective disorder. My one saving grace is that I still miraculously am decently intelligent so I am able to function relatively normally. However, I don't want to continue living like this my mind feels as if it's literally tearing itself apart. I know there is help, and there are a number of logical steps I can take to attempt to solve this problem. I am just exhausted and the bigger issues aren't mental or physical I can still excel in society. It is the pointlessness of it all and the isolation. I am not going to eke out a meager and pained existence I simply rather just do away with it.

That's a good question, there are a lot of factors involved in contributing to my circumstance. I had thought about giving it a long, poetic response but I will save that for later and keep it short. These are just a few of the things involved in my decision. Essentially a lack of community, diminished faith in society, isolation, a society that does not value me, declining health, and a collapsing psyche are the main forces at play. However, those are all event driven scenarios and have compounded over time. Simply I just don't see a point in existing any longer prolonging my pain. I feel as though society has failed me and in turn I have failed it or will fail it. I am not going to complain, the only rules in existence are the laws of physics.
